evidence.quote: Alloy ingots with an intended composition of Al5Mo7Nb36Ti39Hf13 (at. %) were prepared using a vacuum arc melting furnace. Raw materials with a purity greater than 99.95 % by weight were used to produce ingots. The furnace chamber was first evacuated to 3.0 × 10^3 Pa and then filled with argon gas to 0.5 Pa to prevent oxidation. A Ti target was melted to absorb the residual oxygen in the furnace chamber prior to melting the alloy ingot. Each ingot was remelted at least eight times to ensure chemical homogeneity, with magnetic stirring applied to ensure a uniform composition.

The cut pieces were then sealed in vacuum quartz tubes to prevent oxidation during extended heat treatment. These quartz tubes were heat-treated in a muffle furnace for 100 h at 600 ◦C, 700 ◦C, 800 ◦C, and 1000 ◦C, followed by water quenching.

The excellent mechanical properties were primarily attributed to dislocation motion.
GBS and DRX played vital roles in promoting dislocation annihilation and reducing dislocation interactions, thereby reducing flow stress during high-temperature deformation.
An increase in the number of DRX grains in AH1000 led to lower PS strength compared with the AH800 specimen during high-temperature compression.
